open_points.subject: owner authentication
open_points.text: Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token.
open_points.question: What is the owner channel, who issues and revokes the owner's token, and how does the kernel distinguish it from an agent token?
options: A separate owner credential configured by an installation operator
The same token system as agents with an owner role
Authentication asserted by the reverse proxy
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate installation-configured owner credential and authenticate it directly at the MCP boundary.

open_points.subject: agent identity
open_points.text: Holds an agent token configured in the installation; the token says whether the agent may author.
open_points.question: What stable identity does each token carry so that each agent's actions are distinguishable in every record?
options: Each token maps to a unique agent identifier
Tokens record only the may-author bit
The caller supplies an agent identifier separately
open_points.default_guess: Map every token to a unique immutable agent identifier and a may-author flag.

open_points.subject: installation administration
open_points.text: service credentials and tokens live in the installation's protected configuration
open_points.question: Who may create, change and remove credentials, tokens, manifest sources and selected service instances, and through what boundary?
options: An installation operator using an out-of-band procedure
The owner through kernel actions
Host automation outside the product
open_points.default_guess: Treat an installation operator and an out-of-band protected configuration procedure as explicit external actors.

open_points.subject: platform manifest
open_points.text: Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest.
open_points.question: Who supplies the manifest, how the kernel authenticates or trusts it, and when manifest changes become visible are not stated; what is the contract for that external input?
options: A local protected file re-read on every relevant request
A startup snapshot requiring restart
A trusted manifest service queried by the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Use a protected local manifest source and re-read it before proposal, acceptance and invocation checks.

open_points.subject: withheld secret echoes
open_points.text: A service's own answer that echoes one verbatim is withheld
open_points.question: What observable node, run and caller result occurs when an answer is withheld because it contains a credential?
options: Fail the node with a distinct secret-leak refusal
Return only a digest and class
Discard the field and continue with a redacted value
open_points.default_guess: Fail the node and run with a distinct secret-leak reason while recording no secret.

open_points.subject: submission of outside material
open_points.text: Their material stays at a microservice's own intake until the owner or an agent submits it.
open_points.question: Which primary action submits an intake item, what identifier or value it accepts, and what observable record links the submission actor to the service intake record?
options: The run action accepts an intake-record reference as a flow input
A separate submit action exists
An operation node discovers intake records without submission
open_points.default_guess: Make the run action accept a typed intake-record reference and record the authenticated caller as submitter.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP operation set
open_points.text: The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.
open_points.question: How are the listed primary actions add trial case, capture failed execution, release failed run, roll back slot, propose binding, compose/prove flow and refuse effect exposed, since they are absent from the claimed fixed MCP set?
options: They are distinct MCP operations omitted from K-11
They are modes of the named author, try, inspect, activate or approve operations
Some are not remotely callable despite the Primary actions table
open_points.default_guess: Expose each primary action as an explicit typed MCP operation and include it in K-11's fixed set.

open_points.subject: contract-version succession
open_points.text: the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot
open_points.question: What makes a later contract version the slot's current contract version, and what happens to the previous contract version's activation and flows that pin it?
options: Authoring a new contract version immediately makes it current
The owner explicitly activates a contract version
Slots have no single current contract version
open_points.default_guess: Authoring a valid later contract version makes it current while existing runs and flow versions retain their pins.

open_points.subject: refused implementation submission
open_points.text: admission over the whole corpus and, when admitted, activation at once
open_points.question: When submission produces an empty-corpus or failing admission verdict, is the immutable implementation and its evidence stored, and what complete result does the submitting caller receive?
options: Store the implementation and refused verdict but do not activate
Reject the call and store nothing
Store the implementation only, with evidence available through inspection
open_points.default_guess: Store the immutable implementation and its refused admission verdict and return all bounded per-case evidence.

open_points.subject: trial case semantics
open_points.text: add a trial case
open_points.question: What fields constitute a trial case and what determines that an implementation passes it: exact expected output, an expected failure, a predicate, or some other oracle?
options: Input plus exact expected output
Input plus expected success or failure code
Input plus a separately authored validator
open_points.default_guess: Use typed input values plus an exact typed expected output.

open_points.subject: capturing a failed execution
open_points.text: the trial case every later implementation must pass
open_points.question: A failed execution supplies an input but may supply no correct output; how does capture obtain the expected result that later implementations must pass?
options: The caller supplies and validates the expected output during capture
Capture creates a regression case requiring only that the prior failure not recur
Only failures with an already known expected output are capturable
open_points.default_guess: Require the capturing caller to supply a typed expected output and store it with the captured input.

open_points.subject: run inputs
open_points.text: run a flow
open_points.question: What inputs the run action accepts, how they bind to the flow's declared input ports, and who assigns their disclosure classes are not stated; what is the run request?
options: A complete map from named flow input ports to typed values and classes
Only service-record identifiers, with all data fetched by operation nodes
Inputs previously stored under kernel references
open_points.default_guess: Accept a complete named map of bounded typed values, with class labels checked against authenticated-source rules.

open_points.subject: run completion with independent branches
open_points.text: a failed node stops its dependants
open_points.question: Do independent branches continue after a node fails, and when they finish, what determines the run's terminal status and returned outputs?
options: Independent branches finish and the run ends failed
All remaining work stops immediately
The run may succeed with partial failures
open_points.default_guess: Continue independent branches, suppress failed-node dependants, and end the run failed after all runnable branches settle.

open_points.subject: approval when service is unreachable
open_points.text: the effect runs on the exact input shown
open_points.question: The action promises that approval runs the effect, but settled question 14 says an unreachable service leaves the approval valid for resume; what output does the approve action return when no send occurs?
options: A pending run and an unused approval record
An approval result followed by a separate failed send result
The approve call remains open until the send succeeds
open_points.default_guess: Return the approval record and a run now pending for an unreachable service, marking the approval unused.

open_points.subject: standing-grant eligibility
open_points.text: grant a standing approval for a node of a flow's active version
open_points.question: May the owner grant read or draft-write nodes, or only state-transition and external-effect nodes that ordinarily stop for approval?
options: Only state-transition and external-effect nodes
Every non-destructive operation node
Every node, including function nodes
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for state-transition and external-effect operation nodes.

open_points.subject: resolution of an applied unknown outcome
open_points.text: the effect is recorded applied, or not applied; the run continues
open_points.question: If an operation has output ports but its unknown attempt is resolved as applied without a response, what output value feeds dependent nodes so that the run can continue?
options: Such operations may not have downstream outputs
The owner supplies a validated output during resolution
The kernel performs a read-back operation declared by the binding
open_points.default_guess: Forbid downstream dependencies on an effect whose applied outcome can be unknown unless resolution supplies a separately validated output.

open_points.subject: read trace failure
open_points.text: | read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | — |
open_points.question: What happens for an unknown run or trace reference, a released run, or a trace value the caller is not allowed to receive?
options: Return an unknown-reference refusal and redact values by K-14
Return an empty collection
Return records even after release because only spool files are removed
open_points.default_guess: Return unknown-reference for nonexistent records, retain records after release, and apply K-14 to every returned value.

open_points.subject: operation effect classification
open_points.text: Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`.
open_points.question: Which actor or trusted source assigns an operation's effect class, where it is stored, and what prevents an agent from proposing a less restrictive class?
options: The trusted platform manifest declares it and bindings must copy it
The owner assigns it when accepting a binding
The proposing agent assigns it and the owner reviews it
open_points.default_guess: Require the trusted manifest operation record to declare the class and make a binding pin it unchanged.

open_points.subject: idempotency-key declaration
open_points.text: The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key
open_points.question: Where an operation declares its idempotency-key location, which effect classes require it, and how the stable key is derived across approval, resume and resend are not stated; what is the contract?
options: The manifest declares a header or body field and the key derives from run, node and logical attempt
Every effect uses a fixed header defined by the kernel
Each binding defines its own key mapping and derivation
open_points.default_guess: Put a typed key-location declaration in the pinned manifest operation and derive the key from run, node and logical effect attempt.

open_points.subject: schema model and equality
open_points.text: An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema.
open_points.question: What schema language is used, how schemas are canonicalized, and whether sameness means byte identity, canonical structural equality or compatibility are not stated; which definition must proof use?
options: Canonical JSON Schema equality
Identity by stored schema digest
A kernel-specific closed value-schema algebra
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed kernel value-schema algebra with canonical serialization and digest equality.

open_points.subject: map semantics
open_points.text: a map of a node over a collection
open_points.question: What collection types may be mapped, whether order is preserved, how item failures affect other items and the run, and what output schema the map produces are not stated.
options: Ordered list map with fail-independent items and an ordered result
Fail-fast ordered list map
Map over any collection with implementation-defined ordering
open_points.default_guess: Map only ordered bounded lists, preserve order, run independent items, and fail the map if any item fails.

open_points.subject: guard semantics
open_points.text: a guard on a declared closed value
open_points.question: What value the guard examines, how alternatives are declared, whether a default branch is required, and what happens to unselected nodes and outputs are not stated.
options: An enum-valued input selects one exhaustive branch
A boolean selects one branch with an optional else
Any closed-schema value may select a sparse branch map
open_points.default_guess: Use an enum-valued port with exhaustive declared branches and record unselected nodes as skipped.

open_points.subject: function input disclosure limits
open_points.text: The flow proof refuses an edge that would deliver a value to an input accepting less.
open_points.question: Bindings declare the highest class accepted by operation inputs, but no corresponding declaration is specified for function input ports; how can proof check edges into functions?
options: Every function contract input declares its maximum accepted class
Function inputs always accept personal_data
A function's contract has one maximum class for all inputs
open_points.default_guess: Require every function-contract input port to declare its maximum accepted class.

open_points.subject: classification of source and zero-input values
open_points.text: Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`.
open_points.question: Who classifies caller-supplied flow inputs, literals or service references, and what class does a zero-input function's output receive when there is no highest received class?
options: Classes are declared by each flow input and zero-input output port
The authenticated caller supplies the class
All unproven sources default to personal_data
open_points.default_guess: Declare source classes in trusted port definitions and default any otherwise unclassified source to personal_data.

open_points.subject: personal-data digest
open_points.text: it returns the value's digest and class instead
open_points.question: Which digest construction and canonical value representation are used, and is the digest keyed or salted to prevent an agent from guessing low-entropy personal values?
options: A keyed digest over canonical typed bytes
An unkeyed cryptographic hash over canonical bytes
A random opaque value identifier rather than a content digest
open_points.default_guess: Return a keyed digest over canonical typed bytes so agents cannot cheaply test guessed personal values.

open_points.subject: owner value access versus secret withholding
open_points.text: The owner receives every value.
open_points.question: Does the owner receive a service answer that echoes a credential, despite the Actors section saying that answer is withheld, or is the statement subject to a secret exception?
options: Secret detection overrides owner access
Only agents are denied echoed secrets
The whole answer is failed and therefore no value exists to return
open_points.default_guess: Make secret detection override all surface disclosure, including to the owner, and fail the producing node.

open_points.subject: meaning of sole personal-data reader
open_points.text: the owner alone reads them
open_points.question: May agent-written sandbox code and microservice operations receive and process personal_data values, or does 'owner alone' forbid those executions as well as agent-surface disclosure?
options: Only human and agent-surface reading is restricted; sandbox code and services may process it
No function may receive personal_data
Only owner-approved nodes may process personal_data
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the rule as a surface-disclosure restriction while allowing validated services and sandbox executions to process classified values without exposing them to the agent.

open_points.subject: repair context
open_points.text: For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence
open_points.question: Which action requests this repair bundle, who selects the slot, what 'recent' means, and whether inspection may expose other implementation bodies are not stated.
options: A dedicated inspect-repair operation with a fixed count or byte bound
The general inspect action with caller-selected pagination
The kernel automatically pushes a bundle after each failure
open_points.default_guess: Use a general inspect request scoped to one slot with explicit bounded pagination and deny other implementation bodies in that repair view.

open_points.subject: malformed response after an effect
open_points.text: their answers are untrusted data until validated at the port
open_points.question: If a service confirms or performs an effect but its response fails output validation, is the attempt applied, unknown or failed, and may it ever be sent again?
options: Record the effect as applied but fail the node on invalid output
Treat the outcome as unknown
Treat it as failed without permitting automatic resend
open_points.default_guess: Record that the request was sent and the effect may be applied, classify the outcome as unknown unless application is independently certain, and prohibit resend without owner resolution and fresh approval.

open_points.subject: simultaneous wait reasons
open_points.text: A run rests `awaiting_approval`, or `pending` when a service is unreachable or an outcome unknown
open_points.question: When independent nodes simultaneously await approval and an unreachable service or unknown outcome, which single run status and reason are observable?
options: Use a deterministic precedence while preserving all node waits
Represent multiple simultaneous run wait reasons
Prevent parallel progress so only one wait can exist
open_points.default_guess: Use a deterministic aggregate status with pending taking precedence and expose every node-level wait reason.

open_points.subject: business facts in retained edge values
open_points.text: It stores no business fact. ... Values and the records that name them are kept for as long as the kernel keeps its traces; this kernel expires nothing.
open_points.question: Are business-valued edge inputs and outputs retained indefinitely as full values, or does 'stores no business fact' require them to be digests or transient data?
options: Full bounded execution values are retained but are not authoritative business records
Business values are retained only by digest
Only non-business values are retained
open_points.default_guess: Retain full bounded execution values as non-authoritative trace evidence and narrow 'no business fact' to mean no system-of-record business state.

open_points.subject: repository boundary
open_points.text: A second agent with the same access continues the work from the kernel's records, the platform manifest and the repositories alone.
open_points.question: Which repositories are authoritative, who grants agents access, what artifacts must be present there, and whether the kernel reads them are not stated.
options: Agents access source repositories independently; the kernel never does
The kernel exposes repository contents through MCP
Repositories are only operational documentation outside the product promise
open_points.default_guess: Name source repositories as an external read boundary available directly to authenticated agents, with the kernel neither reading nor modifying them.

open_points.subject: effectful-flow rehearsal
open_points.text: Effectful flows are rehearsed on an installation of disposable rigs.
open_points.question: What action performs or records a rehearsal, what observable evidence proves it happened, and what failure prevents use against real instances?
options: Rehearsal is an operational convention with no kernel enforcement
The kernel records a successful rehearsal prerequisite before production activation
Separate installations are manually selected and no promotion relationship exists
open_points.default_guess: Treat rehearsal as an explicit operational acceptance step outside kernel enforcement and remove it as an unqualified kernel guarantee.

open_points.subject: photo-upload acceptance sequence
open_points.text: A flow takes an original invoice photo into custody through the owning service's declared operations; it shows effect classes, the owner's approval on the exact input, the idempotency key and `pending`.
open_points.question: Which operation takes custody, what exact observable result proves custody, which pending reason must be demonstrated, and whether the case must later resolve to a terminal status are not stated.
options: Demonstrate outcome_unknown, resolve it, and verify custody by a service response
Demonstrate service_unreachable and resume
Any pending state is sufficient and no terminal outcome is required
open_points.default_guess: Require a declared custody operation, show an outcome_unknown attempt with its key and approved request, resolve it as applied, and verify a service-owned custody identifier before success.

open_points.subject: real instances versus disposable rigs
open_points.text: both cases pass against the real service instances
open_points.question: Does the effectful photo case run against production-like disposable rigs or persistent real instances, and how is that reconciled with K-16's requirement that effectful flows be rehearsed on disposable rigs?
options: Disposable rigs are the real instances selected for acceptance
Rehearsal runs on rigs and acceptance then repeats against persistent instances
The photo acceptance case does not actually send an effect
open_points.default_guess: Use disposable but fully real service instances as the acceptance installation.

open_points.subject: third-party analysis result
open_points.text: returns an analysis, releasing nothing
open_points.question: What concrete analysis output, correctness oracle and meaning of 'releasing nothing' make this case pass or fail?
options: Compare a typed result to a fixed expected value and require no write-class operation attempts
Require only schema-valid output and no external-effect nodes
Human review decides whether the free-form analysis is acceptable
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed service fixtures and an exact typed expected analysis, with traces proving that only read operations ran and no data left the kernel to a write or external-effect operation.

open_points.subject: one-conversation constraint
open_points.text: Within one conversation the agent writes the missing functions, tries and admits them, composes a read-only flow over declared read operations and returns an analysis
open_points.question: What begins and ends the conversation, whether retries or a second agent are allowed, and which records prove all steps occurred within it are not stated.
options: One MCP client session identified in every request
One external chat thread with no kernel-visible identity
A bounded scripted acceptance scenario, regardless of transport session
open_points.default_guess: Define it as one scripted MCP client session with a correlation identifier recorded on every action.

open_points.subject: negative acceptance inventory
open_points.text: each refusal of K-05 through K-09 is shown by a bounded negative case
open_points.question: What is the authoritative list of refusals to cover, what 'bounded' limits, and what observations constitute a passed negative case?
options: Every explicit refusal and failure branch in K-05 through K-09
One representative refusal per decision
Only the refusal rows in Primary actions
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate every explicit refusal branch in K-05 through K-09 and require a finite fixture, refusal code or reason, unchanged prohibited state and trace evidence for each.

open_points.subject: out-of-kernel photo processing
open_points.text: the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel
open_points.question: Where this processing runs, how the agent obtains and returns the file, and how that path obeys the rules that agents never receive personal_data and callers never receive files are not stated.
options: The statement refers only to an agent-operated external tool with its own trust policy
The owner performs the processing and the agent only directs it
Photos are guaranteed not to be personal_data and may leave through a separate channel
open_points.default_guess: Treat photo processing as outside the product boundary and do not promise it unless a separately named trusted tool and disclosure policy are specified.

open_points.subject: approval request equality and credentials
open_points.text: the fully built request as the owner was shown it — method, URL, headers and body. Any difference at send ... asks again. The credential's value is never shown, so rotating it voids nothing.
open_points.question: How is request equality computed when a credential-bearing header differs but all header differences were said to void approval, and which request fields are designated credentials?
options: Compare a canonical request with credential fields replaced by stable placeholders
Exclude all authorization headers from equality
Pin credential identity but not its secret value
open_points.default_guess: Have the manifest mark credential injection fields and compare a canonical request where each injected credential value is replaced by a stable credential identifier.

open_points.subject: showing multipart file content for approval
open_points.text: the parts themselves — name, filename, media type and content — are what the owner was shown and what must not differ
open_points.question: How is file content shown to and approved by the owner when flow callers never receive files, and is approval tied to bytes, a digest, a preview or another representation?
options: Show metadata plus a cryptographic digest and bind approval to the exact bytes
Transfer the complete file to the owner over MCP
Show a bounded preview while separately binding the unseen remainder by digest
open_points.default_guess: Show metadata and a digest, optionally a bounded preview, and bind approval equality to the exact spooled bytes represented by that digest.
